description: This file defines the 'Feed' class in the Goteo project, managing event logging, retrieval, and display functionalities related to feeds and activity streams.

classes.name: Feed
classes.description: Manages creation, retrieval, and display of activity feed events, including push, fetch, and formatting functions, within the Goteo platform.

methods.name: __construct
methods.description: Initializes the Feed object, translating its title and preparing the HTML body.

methods.name: populate
methods.description: Fills the Feed instance with data such as title, URL, HTML content, and image.

methods.name: getBody
methods.description: Returns the HTML content of the feed, unserializing if necessary.

methods.name: setBody
methods.description: Sets the HTML content, serializing if the input is a FeedBody object.

methods.name: setUnique
methods.description: Marks the feed as unique to prevent duplicates.

methods.name: setTarget
methods.description: Assigns the target object (user, project, call, etc.) and its ID.

methods.name: setPost
methods.description: Associates a blog post ID with the feed event.

methods.name: doEvent
methods.description: Internal method to set scope and type, then add the event.

methods.name: getAll
methods.description: Retrieves all feed events of a specified type and scope, with optional filtering for nodes.

methods.name: getProjUpdates
methods.description: Fetches recent project update feed events.

methods.name: getUserItems
methods.description: Retrieves feed events relevant to a specific user, filtered by type.

methods.name: add
methods.description: Persists the current Feed instance into the database, respecting the 'unique' flag to prevent duplicates.

methods.name: time_ago
methods.description: Converts a timestamp into a human-readable relative time string like '2 hours ago'.

methods.name: item
methods.description: Generates HTML snippet for a feed item label.

methods.name: subItem
methods.description: Generates an HTML representation of a feed event, including avatar, title, timeago, and content.
